exposure: delivery in less than 10 days after diagnosis of preeclampsia (early delivery group)
delivery at 10 days or later after diagnosis of preeclampsia (delayed delivery group)
outcome: significantly preterm delivery (before 34 weeks of gestation)
maternal intensive care or intensive monitoring for more than 24 h
Apgar score of less than seven at five minutes
cohort: The study included 1637 women diagnosed with preeclampsia recruited at five university hospitals in Finland.
finding: Early and delayed delivery after preeclampsia diagnosis lead to comparable maternal and perinatal outcomes in this cohort, with no differences in preterm deliveries, maternal intensive care needs, eclampsia, or fetal death, although low Apgar scores were more common in the early delivery group.
